label: rem:hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction-context
title: Hoefsmit-as-surreal — eigencomponent recursion, tableau counting, and consequences
html:
At each step of the Young--Jucys--Murphy tower, a Hecke generator \sigma_i splits a tableau-vector into two eigencomponents:

  • the symmetric (q-eigen) component, corresponding to the tableau where boxes i and i+1 lie in the same row;
  • the antisymmetric (-q^{-1}-eigen) component, corresponding to the tableau where they lie in the same column.

This is structurally identical to Conway's recursive surreal construction.

Let \mathrm{Tab}(\lambda) denote the set of standard tableaux of shape \lambda, viewed as the vertex set of a tree \mathcal{T}_n whose edges record the Young--Jucys--Murphy ordering. Let \mathbf{No}_{= n}^{\mathrm{dy}} denote the set of dyadic surreals of birthday exactly n (equivalently, sign sequences of length n). The number of two-rowed standard tableaux of size n is \binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}; the number of dyadic surreals of birthday exactly n is 2^n. The embedding \Phi of prop:hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction is an injective embedding, not a bijection of forests.

This identification has several immediate consequences. The sign-sequence braid invariant is well-defined and lives in \mathbf{No}_{\leq c(\beta)}^{\mathrm{dy}} for a braid \beta of crossing number c(\beta). Birthday refines crossing number: b(\mathrm{surr}(\beta, t)) \leq c(\beta), with equality for reduced braids. The Hoefsmit factorisation equals the Conway construction: the closed formula for \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i) as a 2 \times 2 matrix in YJM coordinates is exactly the recursive surreal recipe x = \{x^- \mid x^+\}, with the eigenvalue ratio q : -q^{-1} determining the position of x. The Jones polynomial J_K(q) can be re-expressed as a weighted sum over surreal sign sequences (Jones polynomial birthday refinement). Finally, knot complexity acquires an honest ordinal-valued refinement: knots of unbounded crossing number live at birthdays approaching \omega.

We already use the Hoefsmit seminormal form as the algebraic-combinatorial backbone of the paper. We show that this same backbone is a literal instance of Conway's surreal-number construction. The surreal lift of QOU is not a new structure; it is a different language for what Hoefsmit already provides.
